\title{Counting Sheep Without Waking Them:\\ Thermal Drones for Overnight Flock Census on Upland Pastures}
\author{M\'aire N\'i Fhaol\'ain\thanks{Corresponding author. Supported by the fictional Upland Futures grant UF-0042.} \and J\"org \O{}stergaard \and Fran\c{c}ois Le~Berger}
\date{\today}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Farmers on unfenced upland pastures count their flocks by hand, at dusk, and usually get it wrong. We describe \sys, a census pipeline that flies a small thermal drone over a sleeping flock and counts warm bodies without waking them. Across $41$ nights on three farms, \sys{} agreed with a walked ground count to within \SI{1.8}{\percent}, against \SI{7.4}{\percent} for the farmers' own dusk counts.

A second abstract paragraph explains that the disturbance score stayed below the waking threshold $\wake$ on every night but one, and that the whole pipeline runs on a laptop in the farmyard.
\end{abstract}

\keywords{thermal imaging, livestock census, unmanned aerial vehicles, point-process models}
